questions.stem: A ferry is pulled toward a wharf at \(25\text{ m/min}\). The rope attaches to the ferry \(6\text{ m}\) below the wharf level. When the ferry is \(28\text{ m}\) from the wharf, how fast is the rope being drawn in?
questions.hint: Relate the horizontal distance x, fixed 6 m vertical gap, and rope length r with Pythagoras. Differentiate with respect to time and use dx/dt=−25.

keyPoints.note: This is the rate at which the horizontal distance x is decreasing.
Substitute x=28 only after differentiating the relation between x and r.

steps.explain: Use the Pythagorean theorem for the right triangle formed by the 6 m vertical drop and horizontal distance x to relate the rope length r to x.

steps.explain: Differentiate with respect to time; the vertical separation is constant.

steps.explain: At x=28, the rope length is √820=2√205 m and dx/dt=−25 m/min. The negative sign means r is decreasing.

steps.explain: The question asks for the speed at which the rope is drawn in, so report the positive magnitude.
